categories.fill: Parse `input`, a document with Slots, and fill it with the JSON text of `data` (STXT-TRANSFORM-SPEC §4); the canonical tree of the result must equal the canonical tree of `expected`, compared as a JSON value. The filled document is not validated.
categories.fill-error: Parse `input` and fill it with `data`; the fill must fail, and the first error must carry `error.code` and `error.line` (1-based): the line of the node in `input` or, when `error.in` is `data`, the line in `data`. The codes are provisional while STXT-TRANSFORM-SPEC is in Genesis.
categories.export: `definitions` is a list of sets of definition files, as in the kit. For every set: load it into one provider, parse `input` and export its root node to JSON (STXT-TRANSFORM-SPEC §3.1); the result must equal `expected` as a JSON value: the same members in the same order, the same elements, strings and literals, and numbers with the same text in plain notation (the text fill puts: digits kept, no exponent).
categories.export-error: Same, but the export must fail, and the first error must carry `error.code` and `error.line`: the line of the node. The codes are provisional while STXT-TRANSFORM-SPEC is in Genesis.
categories.import: For every set of `definitions`: import the JSON text of `input` as the node `node` of `namespace` (STXT-TRANSFORM-SPEC §3.2); the canonical tree of the result must equal the canonical tree of `expected`, compared as a JSON value. When `valid` is given, validating the imported node with the recursive validator must give no error (true) or some error (false).
categories.import-error: Same, but the import must fail, and the first error must carry `error.code` and `error.line`: the line in `input` for an error of the JSON text, 0 for the others. The codes are provisional while STXT-TRANSFORM-SPEC is in Genesis.
categories.json: Read the JSON text of `input` with the JSON reader of the transforms (RFC 8259, strict; where RFC 8259 leaves the choice, as JSON.parse, json.loads and Jackson read: the last value of a duplicate key wins, and an unpaired surrogate is kept); it must be accepted, and its value must equal the value of `expected` as `export` compares them.
categories.json-error: Reading `input` must fail, and the first error must carry `error.code` and `error.line` (1-based). The reader rejects what RFC 8259 does not allow and applies the limits of STXT-SPEC §11.2 with their default values. A duplicate key and an unpaired surrogate are not errors (category `json`).

cases.description: The example of the specification, filled as it shows.
A value with no Slots is copied as it is.
The comments do not pass to the filled document.
The namespace stays where the document with Slots declares it.
Fill needs neither a namespace nor a definition, and does not validate: nothing defines com.example.x, and Quantity is not a number.
Every root node is filled.
Strings, numbers and booleans put their text; decimals keep their trailing zeros and nothing is written in exponent form.
A number puts its text in plain notation: an exponent gives the digits it writes, and -0 is 0.
<var> is the value of the node, and the node can have children.
Only blanks can follow <var>.
<var> ends the value: another <var> cannot follow it.
<var> ends the value: text cannot follow it.
<var> ends the value: a [list] cannot follow it.
<var> ends the value also after a [list].
<var> and a text that is only ${var} give the same.
A text can carry several ${var}, and the text around them is copied as it is.
${var} can go in any line of a block.
The name of a Slot has ASCII letters, digits, hyphens and underscores.
What does not have the form of a Slot is text.
A ? outside the delimiters is text: it does not make a Slot optional.
In the text, <x>, [x] and {x} are text, inline and in a block.
Everything with the form ${name} is a Slot, also in a block: ${HOME} expects a data item HOME.
$${ is a literal ${.
$${ is a literal ${, also before what is not a Slot.
A $$ not followed by { is copied as it is.
The name of a <var> is looked up as it is, case-sensitively: <Date> does not find date.
The name of a ${var} is looked up as it is, case-sensitively: ${Date} does not find date.
A ${var} looks up its data item in the current element and then upwards.
In the text, the nearest data item hides the one above.
<var> looks up its data item only in the current element.
[list] looks up its array only in the current element.
{object} looks up its object only in the current element.
An optional Slot of the navigation with no data item in the current element removes the node, even if a level above has one.
In the text, a null counts as absent and ends the lookup.
${?var} puts nothing for a null, even if a level above has the key.
An object applies to the node and to its children.
A null counts as absent.
Every Slot is required: <var>.
Every Slot is required: ${var}.
Every Slot is required: {object}.
Every Slot is required: [list].
<?var> with no data item removes the node, with its children.
<?var> with a data item puts it.
[?list] and {?object} with a data item behave as [list] and {object}.
${?var} with no data item puts nothing, and the node stays.
${?var} with no data item only removes its own piece of the text.
[?list] and {?object} with no data item remove the node, with its children.
{?object} with a null removes the node.
An empty array produces no node and is not an error.
<var> expects a string, a number or a boolean, not an object.
<var> expects a string, a number or a boolean, not an array.
${var} expects a string, a number or a boolean, not an object.
[list] expects an array, not a string.
[list] expects an array, not an object.
{object} expects an object, not a string.
{object} expects an object, not an array.
The data is a JSON text: an unfinished one is an error, at its line in the data.
[list] repeats the node, with its children, once per element.
A list at the root gives several root nodes.
An element that is a value is the value of the node.
An element that is a value is the content of a block, with its line breaks.
A node that takes its value from the list has nothing else: no text.
A node that takes its value from the list has nothing else: no ${var}.
A node that takes its value from the list has nothing else: no children.
A block that takes its content from the list has nothing else: no more lines.
No navigation can follow a list of values: no {object}.
No navigation can follow a list of values: no <var>.
An array that mixes values and objects is an error.
An array inside an array is an error.
A null element is as if it were not there, among values.
A null element is as if it were not there, among objects.
Navigation applies from left to right, and the text follows it.
Navigation applies from left to right, and can end with a <var>.
Each list repeats over what the previous one leaves.
Blanks are allowed between the navigation and before the text.
A tab is a blank between the navigation.
Once the text has started, what would be navigation is text.
A first block line with only navigation applies and is not copied.
A first block line that does not start with navigation is text.
Navigation after the first line of a block is text.
A first block line that starts with something else is text, with its brackets.
A first block line of navigation can have blanks around and between the Slots.
A first block line that starts with navigation has nothing else: no text.
A first block line that starts with <var> has nothing else.
A first block line that starts with navigation has nothing else: no ${var}.
A first block line that looks like navigation and has more is an error.
A Markdown link at the start of a block has the form of a Slot.
<var> is the content of a block, with its line breaks.
${var} as the only line of a block gives the same as <var>.
The first line of a block can repeat and then put the content.
<?var> as the content of a block with no data item removes the block.
<var> as the content of a block is required.
<var> as the content of a block expects a string, a number or a boolean.
A block whose content is <var> has no more lines.
An HTML block cannot start with a tag that has the form of a Slot.
An HTML block can start with <!DOCTYPE html>, which does not have the form of a Slot.
An XML block can start with an XML declaration, which does not have the form of a Slot.
What the data puts is not filled again.
An empty first block line is text.
A blank first block line is text.
A block keeps the indentation of its lines.
The filled node keeps its form: inline stays inline and a block stays a block.
A data item with line breaks is an error in an inline value.
A data item with line breaks is an error in an inline text.
A data item with line breaks gives several lines in a block.
An inline value has no blanks at either end (STXT-SPEC §5.1).
Inside an inline text, the blanks of the data stay.
In a block, the leading blanks of a line and the empty lines in between are content; the trailing blanks (STXT-SPEC §10.2) and the final empty lines (§10.3) are not.
The text around the data is normalized too: an optional Slot with no data item leaves no trailing blank and no final empty line.
An error carries the line of the node it is about.
The example of the specification, exported as it shows it.
Numbers are exported with their value and their digits, the members follow the order of the definition, and a repeatable child is an array.
A block is exported as a string with line feeds, keeping the indentation of its lines.
An export needs the schema of the namespace.
An export of a node that the schema does not define is an error.
An export of a value that does not fit its type is an error.
A node with a value and children is not decided yet, and is an error.
The export of the example comes back with the same tree, and it is valid.
A string, a number or a boolean is accepted for any node with no children, and written as text.
What does not fit its type is imported as text, and the validation of the imported document rejects it.
The keys are matched with the children by their canonical name.
A TEXT, which allows both forms, is inline when inline loses nothing.
A TEXT with line breaks is a block.
A TEXT that starts with blanks is a block, which keeps them.
A node whose type has only the inline form gets a block for a text with lines, and the validation rejects it.
A duplicate key is accepted, and the last value wins.
A node with repeatable children expects an array, not a number.
A node with children expects an object, not an array.
A node with no children expects a string, a number or a boolean, not an object.
A node with no children expects a string, a number or a boolean, not null.
A repeatable child expects an array, not a string.
The root node, with children, expects an object, not an array.
A key that is not a child of its node is an error.
An import needs the schema of the namespace.
An import of a node that the schema does not define is an error.
